text:
maria: Quick follow-up from the infra all-hands Q&A 1 thank you team. Two asks from comms: a short "one-paragraph" customer-friendly note about APAC timing, and a clear bullet summary of user-visible behaviors when a region hits capacity constraints.

sophia: TL;DR for comms: "We're targeting an invite-only APAC pilot in late September. Broader availability is expected in early Q4 subject to hardware deliveries and vendor lead times." Use 'target' and 'subject to supply' language.

joel: For the user-visible behaviors, can infra list the exact sequence of actions the platform takes? CS wants copy they can paste.

sophia: Sequence (short): 1) prefer in-region warm pool replicas 2) if insufficient, activate cross-region warm pool within the same continent 3) if still constrained, route to a lower-memory quantized model variant 4) as last resort, throttle non-critical routes and return 429s for best-effort routes.

lisa: FYI procurement update: vendor D just confirmed a partial APAC shipment arriving ~4 weeks later than planned. That reduces our APAC buffer by ~12% for the next quarter. Posting details to #procurement-watch.

procurement-bot: Vendor D shipment revised: estimated delivery 2142450000. Impact: APAC slot buffer -12%.

arjun: We need latency-impact numbers for each step so product and CS can set expectations. Even roughs are fine for now.

sophia: Rough (p95-ish): in-region warm pool: +10-25ms; cross-region (same continent): +60-180ms depending on distance; quantized variant: +150-350ms and potential small quality regression; throttling: requests may be rate-limited. We'll publish a measured table early next week.

maria: Can we add a short policy statement about Dedicated customers (region pinning) vs Hosted? Legal asked us to be explicit.

sophia: Policy: Dedicated and Private deployments respect region pinning; we will not cross-region failover without explicit customer opt-in. Hosted customers participate in cross-region failover by default. We'll surface a toggle in the account settings.

arjun: For the autoscaler behavior: does the autoscaler prefer maintaining latency SLOs or reducing cost (i.e., reducing warm pools) when incentives conflict? We need the default for e2e tests.

sophia: Default policy: prioritize latency SLOs for priority routes; for non-priority routes prefer cost-saving actions (batching, quantized fallbacks). We'll expose a policy JSON with keys like "latency_priority", "allow_cross_region", "max_cross_region_ms". I'll upload a sample policy.

lisa: Action items from this thread: - publish one-paragraph comms blurb (maria + sophia) - post p50/p95 latency table (sophia, due Mon) - update procurement digest with revised ETA (lisa, due Thu) - add policy JSON sample to docs (sophia, tag arjun) - update runbook thresholds (arjun to PR after sophia numbers).

capacity-bot: Regional snapshot (snapshot ts 2142155600):
US-West: 91%
US-East: 87%
EMEA: 66%
APAC: 38%

maria: Thanks. Small ask: once the one-paragraph blurb and legal-friendly wording are ready, can someone cc exec-comm? We want to align the customer changelog and support scripts.

sophia: Will do. Drafting legal-friendly blurb now and will post here for review.

joel: I'll take the runbook PR once sophia posts the latency numbers and thresholds.

lisa: I'll post procurement details and create the weekly invite for procurement syncs.

maria: Appreciate it. If anyone needs me to merge language for customer emails, ping me and I'll approve. :thumbsup:
